paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: Jesus knows what's coming, and He's in charge of it. He tells two disciples exactly what they'll find, a colt tied in the village, and exactly what to say if anybody asks. It all happens just the way He said (Mark 11:2-6). I can't even predict where I left my own hat, and He's out here scheduling colts!

Now look at what the crowd does with Him. They spread cloaks and branches on the road and shout, "Blessed is He who comes in the name of the Lord!" (Mark 11:9). They call out a blessing on "the coming kingdom of our father David!" (Mark 11:10). This is a welcome fit for a king, and Jesus lets them give it to Him, riding a colt that no one has ever sat on (Mark 11:2, 7).

So what does it mean for you, baker? You can trust a Lord who knows the road ahead, even when your job is just to untie one colt and say what He told you to say. And you can give Him the welcome He deserves, with everything you've got. Spread out your cloak, friend, and let Him lead.
